title: Understanding LLM Agent Behaviours via Game Theory: Strategy Recognition, Biases and Multi-Agent Dynamics

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM behavior in repeated game-theoretic scenarios (Prisoner's Dilemma and Public Goods Game) using identical rules but prompts translated into multiple languages (e.g., English, Vietnamese, Arabic, Chinese, French) to measure differences in cooperation rates and canonical strategic choices.

Injecting explicit 'Cooperative' or 'Selfish' personality traits into agent prompts and measuring how strongly different LLM architectures adhere to or deviate from these instructions, revealing inherent prosocial or instruction-following tendencies.
Comparing the strategic behaviors (e.g., propensity for defection vs. cooperation) of agents based solely on their sequential ordering ('Agent 1' vs. 'Agent 2') within the multi-agent system prompt.
